note: Raw colour-literal audit of frontend/src (hex, rgb/rgba/hsl, named colours; currentColor and comments ignored; styles.css skipped because it holds the token definitions). varRisks lists existing var(--color-*) uses whose meaning flips in dark mode. See docs/THEMING.md.

ink-fill.meaning: background uses var(--color-ink): it becomes LIGHT in dark. Primary/inverse control with ink-contrast text is fine; an always-dark panel must use --term-bg*.

ink-contrast-text.meaning: text uses var(--color-ink-contrast): it becomes DARK in dark. Fine on an ink fill; wrong inside an always-dark panel (use --term-fg).

ink-contrast-fill.meaning: background uses var(--color-ink-contrast): it becomes DARK in dark. Check it is a surface; for a deliberately white card use --color-surface.

accent-fill-text.meaning: accent fill with no color or color: var(--color-ink): ink is light in dark, so lime + light text. Set color: var(--color-on-accent).

shadow-ink.meaning: box-shadow uses var(--color-ink): a white block shadow in dark. Use var(--color-shadow).

ink-on-dark-js.meaning: inline style in JSX/JS uses a flipping token.
